div.head: I Cn 24
div.ab: And we lærað, þæt man wið fúlne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthæmed ⁊ wið æghwylcne æwbryce warnige symle.
And we lærað, þæt man wið fulne galscype ⁊ wið unrihthæmed ⁊ wið æghwylcne æwbrece wærnige symle.
⁊ we lærað, þæt man wiþ fulne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthǽmed ⁊ wið æghwylce ǽwbryce warnian georne.
Et ab inmundis gaudiis (a libidine) et iniusto concubitu uel adulterio caueatur.
⁊ we lærað þæt man wið fulne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthǽmed ⁊ wið æghwylce ǽwbryce warnian georne.
And we lærað þæt man wið fulne galscipe and wið unrihthæmed and wið æghwylcne æwbryce warnige symle.
Und wir schreiben vor, dass man vor schmutziger Geilheit und vor gesetzwidrigem Beischlaf und vor jedem Ehebruch sich stets (ernstlich B) hüte.
And we instruct that people always (eagerly, B) beware of foul lust and unlawful intercourse and every kind of adultery.
And we enjoin that foul lasciviousness and illicit unions and every [kind of] adultery be zealously abhorred.
And we instruct that foul lust, illicit intercourse, and all forms of adultery are to be zealously avoided.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
